recipes.name: Sweet Potato, Carrot, Apple, and Red Lentil Soup
ingredients_raw: 2 large sweet potatoes, peeled and chopped

steps.text: Melt butter in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Add sweet potatoes, carrots, apple, and onion; cook and stir until onion is translucent, about 10 minutes.

Stir in lentils, salt, ginger, pepper, cumin, chili powder, and paprika, then pour in broth. Increase the heat to high and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until lentils and vegetables are soft, about 30 minutes.

Purée soup in the pot with an immersion blender until smooth. Increase the heat to medium-high and cook until simmering, about 10 minutes. Add water as needed to thin the soup to your preferred consistency.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Potato, Carrot, Apple, and Red Lentil Soup
raw_recipe.description: This carrot, apple, sweet potato, and lentil soup seasoned with ginger, cumin, and chili powder is full of flavor — it warms you up on a cold winter day!

video.description: This bright soup has all the vegetables you love! Sweet potatoes, carrots, apples, and red lentils give this cozy soup a great color!

review.reviewBody: There are two good reasons why this recipe is a 5-star meal: First, at any given time, the average health-conscious person has all of these ingredients in her kitchen, which makes it so convenient. And second, the flavors and spices are spot on! I've made it several times as is and I feel like I can now mention my own twists on the original. One, replace the butter with equal amount coconut oil for a healthier fat and complimentary flavor with the ginger. Two, don't puree it! It is such a pretty stew as is! And three, the last five minutes of simmering, throw in about 4 cups of fresh, chopped spinach for a boost in color and nutrients. Take my word for it--this recipe is worth making!

I’ve made this recipe before and loved it, but it does take a long time. Today I tried it in my instant pot, and am very happy with the results. There’s a lot of chopping, so I started the onions and butter on sauté mode while I chopped the rest of the ingredients and added them to the pot, stirring occasionally. Deglazed with the broth and added lentils last. I pressure cooked for five minutes. It was actually too long, and next time I will do three minutes. I will also try coconut oil instead of butter because I think it would add to the flavor. Didn’t bother to purée. Super happy with how fast it was!

This is my family's favorite soup. We have been making it multiple times a year for over fifteen years now! The only changes we make are using olive oil instead of butter, and not pureeing (or pureeing only a little bit). Over the years, we've made double, triple, and even quadruple batches; we've left out the onions because of dietary restrictions; we've frozen it, traveled to family's houses hours away with it, and brought it to work potlucks; we've added more or less of the veggies or broth to match what we had available or stretch the soup to feed more folks. It never misses. Always filling and richly flavorful, and without fail, at least one person always asks for the recipe. Thank you for giving us this family staple!

Used only 1 tsp margarine instead of 1/4 cup butter. Sautéed 2 cloves garlic and onion then added yams which I had first chopped and microwaved until soft. Double cumin, add cinnamon &nutmeg. 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes. No salt.added zucchini. 2 small cans lentils. Hand Blended yams and lentils/ soup briefly to make partially smooth.

Very tasty. I used instant pot as I am trying to use it more. Used a little oil instead of butter and then mostly water sauté of vegetables in sauté mode then pressure cooked on “soup/broth” mode low, which was about 6 minutes and since I was going out for a walk, I set it to slow cooker mode after that. Finished with my immersion blender and done. No yogurt needed. Followed directions for content and very good.

I loved this soup! I must admit that I made a few minor changes. One was a senior moment when I grabbed the curry powder instead of the chili. I'm sure that it is good with chili, but let me tell you, the curry really enhanced the flavor of with rest of the ingredients. The second change was opting for butternut squash to supplement 1 lonely little sweet potato. I wasn't going out to the store for another. Again, a win as far as flavor. Lastly, as a preference, I used a potato masher to crush some of the vegetables. I like chunky soup and the partially mashed ingredients still gave it a creamy texture. A fabulous soup for a cold, winter's day.

I just used the recipe as a suggestion...LOL I added curry,tumeric and a bit of masala spice.less butter and used coconut oil.. I also used already cooked left over sweet potato and a huge can of red lentil soup---which made it so much faster to make....I didn't make it a totally smooth soup but left some chunks of carrot etc. I put a dollop of garlic spread on top and OMG! Can't wait to have a second helping!!! Sooooo Delish!

Oh my, I LOVE LOVE LOVE this recipe! I've made it 100 times and it is so nourishing and hearty. With some toast points it's a great little meal. It's obviously perfect in the fall but I make it all year long, and usually end up freezing half of it for another meal. 

I cut the butter in half and then add a little chix stock when I cook the veggies. It's fun to play with the spices a bit too...In addition to the recipe, today I made it with a touch of Chinese 5 star, Garam Masala, Cinnamon, allspice, cloves, smoked paprika as well. I put in a ton of ginger - maybe 2 Tbsp. A big minced clove of garlic is also added. All in all it just rounds out the flavor. 

On top I'll put some fresh chives or maybe a little parsley with the fat free greek yogurt. This recipe is literally in the top 3 of all recipes I make. Nothing like a thick soup in the fall and winter.

Was absolutely a WINNER!!!! Instead of butter, I op for 2 tbs of coconut oil. Also add 1C of red lentil instead of 1/2 and a 1/8 tsp of turmeric. Will definitely used this recipe again. Husband and guests singing praises to the perfect thickness of the soup as well as the flavour. Many thanks.

This is fabulous. I should have taken a photo before it was gone.

I am adding tips because an advertisement covered this part . So - puree in batches (I have a vitamix but I am certain a high speed blender is fine). Make sure each batch is smooth is smooth. Pour each batch into a large clean pot and simmer over medium heat. Add water, as needed.

This is worth all the peeling and chopping; enjoy.

This soup is so wonderful! Since I planned to puree the soup, I left the peel on the apple, and it just blended right in. I did not have fresh ginger, so I used 1/8 tsp of dried, as well as no paprika, so I used 1/4 tsp of za'atar. Delicious on its own, but amazing with a dollop of sour cream stirred in!
I made it as per the recipe , it is delicious, I did add a dollop of sour cream to my bowl
It wasn't difficult to make and tasted amazing. I love it!

Easy to make, freezes very well. Wrangling the butternut squash was the hard part but I think frozen would ease the task. Delicious as written. Great source of protein and fiber. Two thumbs up, it would be more thumbs if there were more hands.
Super easy and quick recipe. I added a full teaspoon of each seasoning and a few garlic cloves.
Soo delicious. I added more seasoning than stated, but everyone has a different preference for intensity. Easy to make and a great filling and nutritious meal.
I like all the ingredients. For me it was too sweet and would leave out the apple next time.
Yummy

I made this soup many years ago when my husband his sister and her husband and I would go hiking the Scottish Highlands. It was an absolute hit and my sister in law always refers to it as Eileen’s soup. She now makes it every week in the winter. I have since moved away from Scotland but visited last week and she reminded me of it. I lost the recipe but she sent it to me and I’m just after making it. Delicious. Especially with my oatmeal bread
My husband and I loved this soup. It’s been so cold here and it hit the spot!
